scope: Human-reviewed static contracts with source anchors. Stage 3 node-copy and UV lifecycle boundaries have isolated ASan/Debug CRT evidence; full application and parallel paths remain unqualified.

contracts.statement: The configuration entry point validates input and copies RuntimeConfig values into process globals before invoking GeneratorAdaptive through synthetic legacy arguments.
contracts.limits: Re-entrant independent configurations are not established; extracting a context is stage 6 work.

contracts.statement: In serial Execute, Geometry and Model are stack objects; Model borrows geometry_ and its destructor deletes pointers stored in meshes_.
contracts.limits: Model copy safety and all alternative MPI/model-loader lifetime routes are not qualified.

contracts.statement: Geometry owns points, vectors, curves and patches with unique_ptr containers. InsertCurve/InsertPatch consume exclusive ownership on entry, including failed insertion; raw arguments are wrapped before container allocation. Failure preserves existing entries and destroys the relinquished argument. Successful insertion preserves pointer identity/order; null adds an empty slot. InsertCurves consumes an ordered pending batch; reserve prepares storage before any append, so failure preserves existing entries and destroys the batch. Successful append moves owners without moving the actual curve objects.
contracts.limits: Arguments must be uniquely owned and deletable through the base pointer; duplicate/aliased adoption is invalid. Scoped allocation-denial and fresh-argument retry cover initialized parametric/Bezier/Hermite copies and patches only. A failed argument is destroyed, not reusable. Generator clone-helper/policy integration, multi-object publication/graph rollback, other constructors/mutations and observers surviving Geometry destruction remain unqualified. Batch qualification covers the clone-publication consumer with zero/one/two clones per source; theoretical max-size overflow is guarded but not dynamically exercised.

evidence.anchor: Consume exclusive ownership, including on failure.

contracts.topic: Physical mesh ownership and node copy
contracts.statement: MeshAdaptive owns SubMesh objects; SubMesh owns nodes/elements. SetNoh copies ID, position and curvature state into an independent node, clearing foreign element observers. AddNoh transfers unique ownership and preserves identity; SetElement adopts its pointer. MeshAdaptive raw SubMesh insertions consume exclusive ownership on entry, before vector growth or position validation. Growth failure leaves existing slots unchanged and destroys the argument; negative positions leave the container unchanged and destroy the consumed argument. Success preserves identity/order and sparse null slots, replacing and destroying any old item.
contracts.limits: The source of SetNoh remains caller-owned. Only this boundary and local reconstruction/move/replacement are instrumented; general NodeAdaptive value copies and full mesh lifecycles remain separate. MeshAdaptive adoption requires uniquely owned actual SubMesh objects, nonthrowing destructors and no duplicate/re-adopted aliases; SubMesh is not polymorphically deletable. Failure consumes the argument; no reuse of that pointer is valid. Existing graph identity, node adjacency and analytic triangle area, allocation-denied growth, negative/null/nonallocating paths and container move/removal are qualified by isolated actual-unit probes. Successful replacement/removal invalidates foreign observers; caller rebinding is not automatic. SubMesh::SetElement raw adoption, other constructors, full-process/parallel memory and logical rejection remain separate.

contracts.statement: TriangleAdaptive borrows three NodeAdaptive pointers, registers itself in each adjacency and caches normal, area and angles. NodeAdaptive adjacency is an observer list.
contracts.limits: General node copies retain observer lists; SubMesh::SetNoh explicitly clears them. Triangle removal, ReplaceNode, coordinate mutation, cache refresh and wider destruction paths remain unqualified.

contracts.statement: Patch stores a non-owning current SubMesh pointer and SubMesh stores a non-owning Patch pointer. PatchCoons borrows Geometry-owned curves.
contracts.limits: Replacing a submesh invalidates old observers; rollback must rebind every patch before the next adaptation.

contracts.statement: Geometry reuses matching four-control Bezier curves in direct or reverse direction. CurveAdaptive does not delete its sampled points; its point and patch lists are observers. SetPoints and UpdateParameters each commit their prepared by-value list by swap; allocation failure preserves that live list and its element nodes. Successful replacement preserves ordered pointer/value results and invalidates old list-element observers without deleting borrowed points or patches. Initialized non-null pointer-taking parametric, Bezier and Hermite copies preserve parameter values/order in independent list nodes alongside the same borrowed sampled points and patches. CloneCurveForPatch returns a pending unique owner through target-incidence insertion. The synchronization-disabled consumer prepares all clones per original curve before batch publication and nonallocating incidence commit; failure preserves the failing curve and any already committed prefix, and whole-operation retry is supported within the qualified graph fixtures. The target-count rebuild helper prepares unique replacement nodes and both the supplied point list and curve parameter list before nonallocating paired swaps and old-interior deletion. Failure preserves both lists, element nodes and old samples; consumed manager IDs remain consumed and retry uses the subsequent IDs. Successful growth preserves uniform parameter formulas and endpoint objects; shrinking preserves rounded index selection and original paired values. The identical construction tails of both serial Adapter methods delegate to BuildCurveSamples. New endpoint/interior nodes, parameters, cache changes and the return list are prepared under exclusive pending ownership. Commit occurs only after return construction succeeds: prepared map nodes merge without allocating, existing cache entry nodes remain stable, parameters swap and new owners release. Failure preserves borrowed samples, curve point observers, parameter list nodes and cache nodes/values; consumed IDs remain consumed. Endpoint scalar/adjacency copy, cached reuse and alias-overwrite policies are preserved. Generator delegates its serial curve/surface/optional-rebuild publication sequence to RefineCurveSamples. A collective RAII transaction prepares equivalent working lists and a cache-value snapshot before parking original point/parameter list nodes. Returned sample lists enter ownership through nonthrowing move assignment before point-observer copies. Failure removes new cache keys, restores existing values in place, deduplicates and reclaims new nonborrowed samples, and restores the original point/parameter nodes. Success deletes superseded first-pass interiors without allocating and transfers final samples to the existing collective graph lifetime. IDs consumed before failure remain consumed; retry uses the subsequent sequence. The serial AdaptCurve scope now uses CurveSampleGraphTransaction across preparation, policy calculations and the complete curve loop. All equivalent working point/parameter lists and the deduplicated initial sample inventory are prepared before original list nodes are parked. Initial samples remain alive across committed per-curve prefixes. Failure clears the operation-local cache, deletes every newly published sample once without allocating, and restores every original point/parameter list node and shared sample object. Success retires the collectively owned initial samples once after the complete loop, leaving final samples under the existing caller graph lifetime. Consumed IDs are not rewound. Serial Generator gives the currently published sample graph one CurveSampleLifetime scope owner before initialization. Normal explicit release and exceptional destruction clear every shared alias before deleting each object once without allocating. Inner sample graph guards unwind before the outer lifetime owner; fatal CLI exceptions do not introduce metadata recovery or retry. Serial InitialMesh delegates to BuildInitialSubMesh, which owns its pending SubMesh, unpublished samples, center temporary and triangles. The first successful curve insertion transfers a sample to the existing collective owner; element insertion consumes a unique owner. Only complete construction publishes the patch observer and returns an owned mesh. The raw compatibility wrapper releases to its valid presized caller.
contracts.limits: Legacy proximity-based matching and sample ownership are not replaced by this inventory; snapshot restoration retains collective sample ownership and recreates nodes explicitly on success, preparing the complete point graph before committing; C12 defines the measured failure boundary. The two setters are independent transactions, not a paired point/parameter transaction. Successful list-node reuse is not promised; redundant copy allocations are removed and old nodes are destroyed after swap. Pointer-taking copy qualification covers initialized scalar/matrix/control state, consistent empty/forward/reversed sampled sequences, independent containers and caller-owned objects; it does not repair inconsistent sources or qualify null/uninitialized sources, implicit copy/assignment, full CLI policy integration or full-process/parallel behavior. Dedicated graph qualification covers initialized base/parametric/Bezier/Hermite curves and real PatchBezier incidences, including repeated edges, null filtering, mixed/non-Coons incidents and committed prefixes. It preserves the pre-existing policy, including mixed-type quirks; it does not establish whole-operation atomicity, adaptive rollback, implicit copies, arbitrary custom subclasses or full-application execution with synchronization disabled. Paired rebuild qualification is limited to initialized parametric/Bezier/Hermite curves and distinct, exclusively deletable removable interiors; borrowed shared endpoints survive. Growth preserves the original uniform-parameter behavior even for reversed input; this is not approval of inconsistent parameter/endpoint geometry. Successful removal invalidates external observers. The curve point-observer list and subsequent Generator SetPoints publication are outside this helper transaction, as are full AdaptCurve, ID rollback, arbitrary/custom allocators/subclasses, manager overflow/wrapping and full mesh rollback. BuildCurveSamples requires initialized parametric/Bezier/Hermite curves, at least two captured points/selected parameters, valid borrowed NodeAdaptive endpoints/cache values and a live manager. The caller retains the existing collective result lifetime/deletion convention. Evaluator scratch changes are not rolled back. This boundary begins after upstream point sorting and parameter selection and ends before Generator point publication; full serial Adapter/AdaptCurve/mesh rollback is unqualified. Endpoint clones still carry copied adjacency observers, without making them owners. Retention-only probes measure leaks after reclaiming reachable partial original state without a preservation/retry claim. Return-move coverage disables optional NRVO consistently only for the new target; debug iterator metadata, extreme/invalid sources, allocator/comparator substitution and manager overflow remain outside qualification. Per-curve publication qualification uses actual template/guard/sample/rebuild units with controlled parameter callbacks and upstream list mutation; it is not full historical Adapter/Generator instrumentation or upstream numerical selection qualification. Initial curve samples and preexisting cache values are borrowed. Sample-tail passes may insert keys/overwrite values but must not erase entry cache keys; rebuild requires distinct exclusively deletable interiors. No concurrent intermediate observer consumption or custom destructive callbacks. Original list nodes are parked until completion; success invalidates those observers. Earlier successful curves, initial graph cleanup on a later failure, evaluator scratch, whole AdaptCurve, mesh/patch/error/history/budget rollback and full-process memory remain open. Preparation changes allocation timing/counts/bytes and peak storage, without a performance claim. Complete point/parameter graph qualification requires fixed curve topology, initialized actual parametric curves, live exclusively deletable collective samples with no competing Geometry control-point or physical mesh owner, nonthrowing destructors and the qualified serial sample/publication/rebuild paths. These paths must keep initial objects alive and publish all newly retained samples in current graph lists. Inner per-curve guards unwind before outer graph cleanup; no stale intermediate observer consumption or concurrent access is permitted. Controlled four-curve loops and actual helpers are instrumented, not the full historical Generator/Adapter translation units or upstream numerical selection. Empty geometry is a guard only. Closed/reversed fixtures preserve ownership and original policy without certifying geometric consistency. Evaluator scratch and orchestration metadata/error/history/budget, patch/mesh/acceptance rollback and full-process/parallel/LSan/UBSan remain unqualified. Resource timing/counts/bytes/peak storage change; no performance claim. Scoped terminal release requires Geometry to outlive its owner, exclusively deletable reachable samples, nonthrowing destructors, independent physical mesh copies and qualified inner publication/graph operations. Controlled initialized three-curve fixtures with shared or distinct endpoints qualify terminal abort, inner graph unwinding and allocation-denied release; they do not instrument the whole Generator/CLI or unpublished constructor allocations. No performance claim for worst-case quadratic alias scanning. Numerical rejection/retry and parallel cleanup are unchanged. Initial-mesh qualification covers actual Bezier planes/bilinear surfaces and fresh/alternating/already-initialized curve layouts, ordered node/element ID channels, reversal and every observed allocation ordinal. Failure preserves the previous patch SubMesh observer, destroys private resources and allows the collective owner to release published prefixes; no curve/scratch/ID rollback or exceptional retry. Fixture setup, custom patches, OpenMP initialization, general raw mesh adoption and whole-process memory remain unqualified.

contracts.statement: Each patch incidence maps local t to canonical t or 1-t; control construction, adaptive boundary traversal and physical edge intervals consume that direction.
contracts.limits: Canonical curve storage does not introduce welding or a new boundary-generation technique.

contracts.statement: Adapter creates old 2D faces from each physical triangle’s stored UV, seeds current boundary vertices from canonical samples, executes CRABMesh, maps new interior vertices through PatchCoons::Parameterize and preserves UV on output triangles.
contracts.limits: Parametric vertices and physical nodes have distinct identity/units and must not be merged into a universal mesh.

contracts.statement: Default AdvancingFront allocates Boundary/Quadtree. Quadtree owns generated template vertices, edges and faces until an allocation-free ordered splice transfers them to front owner lists. It destroys any untransferred template payload on failure or abandonment before deleting its root/boundary. Default front construction guards Boundary until Quadtree construction completes; failure before adoption leaves no retained boundary. TemplateStorage owns unregistered template buffers/objects and releases only successfully registered prefixes to Quadtree. Outer creation uses local vertex/edge guards until registration. Initial root extents stay locally owned until root construction succeeds. Midpoint buffers and all five vertices remain locally owned until complete construction; successful allocation and subdivision order is unchanged.
contracts.limits: Getters return borrowed pointer views; template owner getters are empty after transfer. External-pointer constructor/setter replacement, mate-root sharing, full-process cleanup remain unqualified. After a template creation exception, the tree is qualified for destruction only; observer consumption and same-tree retry are not supported by this slice. Prepared fixture covers types 1 and 4, not all patterns. Root-only generation, one uniform subdivision, edge/old-face generation and prepared neighbor refinement are allocation-failure destruction controls; failed trees must not be queried or retried.

contracts.statement: Edge/Face destructors retain legacy endpoint ownership outside shared containers. Boundary, Quadtree and front cleanup call DetachVertices without allocating; Face detachment releases a midpoint alias to an endpoint while preserving distinct cache ownership. Edge/Face setVertices prepare owned caches before committing endpoints; allocation failure preserves live state. Face cache replacement preserves an old endpoint-alias midpoint as borrowed. Boundary registration guards temporary vertices/edges and commits IDs/contour state only after owner nodes succeed, rolling back edge observers on failure. Face::quality owns temporary centers and detaches its borrowed-endpoint edge on unwind. Public subdivision queries require an attached quadtree and throw std::logic_error when it is missing; owned-cell numerical criteria remain unchanged. Edge::angle(Vertex*, Vertex*) also detaches its temporary borrowed endpoints on every exit, including allocation failure during cache construction/reset or copied adjacency. Edge::makeParamMid prepares an owned replacement and normalized length before committing either; allocation failure preserves the old cache identity/geometry and edge state. Successful replacement delays old-cache destruction until preparation completes and invalidates old cache observers.
contracts.limits: Conditional detachment remains explicit; normal, partial, failed/exceptional post-template exits and selected transfer-allocation failures are isolated controls, not universal observer ownership or arbitrary exception safety. New setter endpoints must not alias a distinct cache owned by that object. Generic individual setters, parametric midpoint replacement and template/Boundary registration failures are not covered by the primitive slice. Registration controls use a null-curve fixture and a quadtree prepared through the real front generate/refine sequence; they do not qualify curve-internal failures, arbitrary setters or all helper paths. Angle-helper qualification covers four endpoint-match branches and the nonadjacent branch with empty/populated caller adjacency; it does not qualify every helper or curve operation. Parametric replacement controls cover four sides in both incidence directions, two interior fallbacks and a null-curve no-op. Curve evaluation scratch remains mutable. Zero observed allocations in the measured polynomial evaluation/integration/bisection do not establish curve-internal allocation-failure coverage; other curve mutation, initialization and shared samples remain unqualified.

contracts.statement: Generator captures ordered curve point ID/XYZ and calls the extracted restoration before retries and after rejection. Restoration prepares unique NodeAdaptive owners by first-encounter ID and all point lists before nonallocating list swaps, owner release and deletion of each unique old sample. Allocation failure preserves live sample objects, list nodes and observers; a later retry is supported. Success preserves the existing first-ID values, order/sharing and zero-initialized node curvature/adjacency.
contracts.limits: Current samples must be initialized, non-null, collectively exclusively owned and deletable through the curves, without competing owners or throwing custom destructors. Success invalidates old sample/list-element observers; raw pointer stability is not promised. Null geometry or snapshot-count mismatch is a no-op. Duplicate IDs retain the original first-encounter behavior, not an endorsement of conflicting coordinates. Parameters are neither captured nor restored. Independent accepted mesh copies remain unchanged in the qualified fixtures; patch binding, mesh/error/history/budget state and full adaptive rollback are separate and unqualified. Full-application/parallel behavior, arbitrary subclasses and inconsistent sources remain open.

contracts.statement: Generator retains saved accepted and rejected meshes via unique_ptr; SaveMesh observes the candidate before later rollback. Adapter returns the selected attempt via release().
contracts.limits: Saving a rejected candidate does not accept it; holding more meshes changes retention/peak-memory behavior and is not permission to prune the scientific trace.

contracts.statement: CurvatureAnalytical evaluates surface derivatives after FindUV; CurvatureDiscrete uses physical-node triangle adjacency, areas and angles.
contracts.limits: Analytical and discrete curvatures are different quantities used for error/adaptation; consolidating their formulas would change the technique.

contracts.statement: Adapter and AdvancingFront both compute face quality statistics, while Generator computes physical mesh statistics. These measurements can refer to different stages and coordinate spaces.
contracts.limits: Shared aggregation is only a future candidate after domains, thresholds, degenerate handling and floating-point ordering are proved equivalent.

contracts.statement: Central definitions expose Eigen fixed-size aliases; PatchBezier evaluation and inverse mapping use matrix operations. CRABMesh also has root-finding numerical helpers.
contracts.limits: No alternative solver or Eigen deletion is authorized by this inventory; stage 5 requires analytic and aliasing/differential comparisons.

contracts.statement: Several patch/Bezier control setters assign point members without rebuilding coefficient matrices; curve setters differ in whether length is recomputed.
contracts.limits: This statically visible mutation contract is not evidence of a current serial CLI regression. Define immutability or explicit rebuild and test it before reuse.

contracts.statement: CMake defines AP_MESH_HAS_OPENMP/AP_MESH_HAS_MPI, while production branches use USE_OPENMP/USE_MPI with false defaults.
contracts.limits: No bridge appears in indexed production files; external defines may alter this. Stage 4 must qualify effective preprocessing and routing, not merely successful linkage.

contracts.statement: Timer accumulates gettimeofday-based intervals; Data::time uses platform-dependent implementations.
contracts.limits: Current clock resolution/monotonicity and performance comparability are not qualified; no speedup claim follows from this inventory.

contracts.statement: AdvancingFront executes old-mesh quadtree generation, neighbor refinement, optional templates, geometric front with conditional topology fallback, then fill and improvement. Generator adapts shared curves before patch interiors and evaluates candidates before acceptance/rollback.
contracts.limits: This ordering is a preservation constraint, not a proposed replacement algorithm.

contracts.statement: Serial mesh export deduplicates submesh node incidences by logical global node ID; pointer equality or close XYZ is not the export identity. Local front IDs and physical IDs use different contexts.
contracts.limits: Boundary copies may share a logical ID across submeshes; conflicting coordinates for one ID are invalid. Proximity matching during input must not silently become export welding.

contracts.statement: PatchCoons(PatchCoons*) invokes only its Patch base copy path and leaves its curve vector default-constructed; the pointer-taking Bezier copy separately copies control/matrix/direction fields.
contracts.limits: These paths are not a qualified complete geometry clone; no current serial CLI failure is inferred. Copy/observer semantics need separate tests before reuse or ownership consolidation.
